summary: Supply-chain pinning (ADR-0055, TM-16). In ci.yml, live-memory.yml and security.yml every third-party action moves from its major tag to the commit SHA of the current release (checkout v7.0.1, setup-python v7.1.0, setup-go v7.0.0, upload-artifact v7.0.2; each SHA equals the current v7 tag, so behaviour is unchanged); threat-model.yml, threat-review.yml and trusted-security-gate.yml were already pinned and are untouched. govulncheck goes from @latest to v1.9.0 and pip-audit to ==2.10.1. pip-audit now also audits router/requirements-session.txt, requirements-dev.txt, test/requirements-hindsight.txt and rerank-server/requirements.txt (all clean locally); the rerank server's exact pins are audited with --no-deps --disable-pip because they need Python >= 3.12 (numpy 2.5.4) while the job runs 3.11, so its transitive dependencies are not audited; decision-jevlike stays out because it installs a git dependency and an unpinned transformers stack (noted). monitoring/compose.yaml pins prom/prometheus:v3.15.1 and grafana/grafana:13.3.0 to their multi-arch index digests, verified equal to the RepoDigests of the containers running in the reference deployment, so a redeploy changes nothing. The decision-service Dockerfiles pin python:3.11-slim to its index digest. Dependabot gains docker-compose (/monitoring) and docker (decision services). test/check_pinned_references.py enforces the rule in CI (workflow actions, go install, pip tools, compose images, Dockerfile FROM) with a self-test of rejected and accepted forms. Permissions, triggers, secrets and job logic are unchanged; the ADR-0050 Dependabot exemption parser accepts the SHA-plus-version-comment form, so future action bumps keep that path. Workflow and review-policy changes should still be looked at by the maintainer. Stacked on that change: router 0.19.1 makes its files owner-only and adds a secret-canary test (ADR-0056, TM-15). common.open_private opens with O_CREAT mode 0600 and fchmods an existing file to 0600 where available; it replaces open() at all seven router write sites (audit log, journal append and compaction, registry, UI overrides with token hashes, save_json_file users such as metrics, fallback observations). Errors still surface as OSError to the same except OSError boundaries as before. The systemd unit adds UMask=0077. test/selftest_log_hygiene.py runs the real API and control apps in-process with canaries (wrong/valid client token, wrong/valid control password, a prompt on the Ollama and OpenAI paths, a token rotated through POST /admin/clients/<name>/token) and searches every captured log record, audit.jsonl, events.jsonl and roles.yaml after confirming the events were recorded; on POSIX it checks the 0600 modes and the tightening of a pre-existing 0644 file. Audit field content is unchanged (no prompts, no tokens; rotation logs only an 8-character hash prefix).

findings.evidence: Before: 23 movable references (actions by tag in three workflows, govulncheck@latest, unversioned pip-audit, two compose images and two base images by tag); pip-audit covered only router/requirements.txt.
findings.resolution: Pinned and enforced in CI; optional requirement sets audited. Hash-locked Python installs and release provenance remain open, so TM-16 stays open in the register.

findings.evidence: Router 0.19.0 created audit.jsonl, events.jsonl and roles.yaml with the process umask (0644 observed under Linux in the negative check); the no-secrets rule for logs was untested.
findings.resolution: Owner-only files in code and unit umask, CI canary test; rotation, backups and independent retention remain open, so TM-15 stays open.

limitations: The new pip-audit loop and the docker/docker-compose Dependabot ecosystems are first exercised in CI and on GitHub.
The decision-service images were not rebuilt with the pinned base image.
decision-jevlike requirements are not audited (git dependency, unpinned transformers stack); hash-locked Python installs and release provenance remain open.
rerank-server: only its exact pins are audited (--no-deps --disable-pip), not their transitive dependencies.
The canary test covers authentication, inference without a node and token rotation; memory, session and upstream error paths are not covered.
